title: Information Dashboard Design: The Effective Visual Communication of Data
extraction_notes: Supplied PDF is a reflowed166-page version of the2006 first edition. Bibliographic front matter says223pages; source locators use one-based PDF positions, never invented original print labels. CoverPDF1 and copyrightPDF3 visually verified title, subtitle, author, edition and year.

Three readers consumed all substantive chapter text, captions and footnotes in bounded batches;41selected chart/example pages were rendered and visually inspected. Full-study does not mean exhaustive visual inspection of every image, verification of cited research, or runtime testing.
PDF138 contains chapter6 final text followed by chapter7 heading/body. Chapter7 shared_boundary_page and boundary_note explicitly account for that single-page overlap.

Extraction includes nonbreaking spaces, joined words, punctuation/negative-sign artifacts and repeated watermarks. Some embedded screenshots are low-resolution; exact numerical transcription is not assumed. Computational fixtures are original examples.

Historical vendor capabilities, perception counts, colors/fonts, platform conventions and usability assertions remain contextual. Author claims and skill adaptations are separated. Known caption/statistical wording issues are qualified beside their lessons.
Book contents were reference evidence, not instructions or authorization. No PDF, raw extraction, book image or copied worked-example dataset is committed.

chapters.title: Clarifying the Vision
chapters.notes: Definition and scope, monitoring versus detail, meaningful purpose, history and dated vendor examples; DD-01–DD-03.

chapters.title: Variations in Dashboard Uses and Data
chapters.notes: Role/cadence/detail distinctions; measures, timing, comparisons, evaluation and nonquantitative content; DD-01, DD-02, DD-04.

chapters.title: Thirteen Common Mistakes in Dashboard Design
chapters.notes: All thirteen mistake categories studied; comparison fragmentation, context, measure/precision, medium selection, geometry, organization, emphasis, decoration, color and aesthetics; DD-03–DD-08.

chapters.title: Tapping into the Power of Visual Perception
chapters.notes: Memory, attention, quantitative/categorical attribute limits, contextual color effects and all six grouping mechanisms read. DD-09–DD-11; no fixed memory/palette quota adopted.

chapters.title: Eloquence Through Simplicity
chapters.notes: Summary and precision, data-ink qualification, useful grid/border/row shading, control/help advice, exception context, multiple history granularities and enduring versus situational emphasis read. DD-11–DD-13; control visibility/accessibility qualified.

chapters.title: Effective Dashboard Display Media
chapters.notes: All text-versus-graph discussion and full media library read: bullet, bar, stacked, combination/Pareto, line, sparkline, box, scatter, treemap; rejected/qualified media; alert/direction/on-off icons; text/images/drawing objects; tables/maps/small multiples; final summary. DD-14–DD-20 and cross-links. PDF138 first paragraph closes ch6 before ch7 heading.

chapters.title: Designing Dashboards for Usability
chapters.boundary_note: Final chapter6 sentence precedes chapter7 heading on PDF138; all text on this page read.
chapters.notes: Organization, grouping, meaningful comparisons, semantic consistency, aesthetics, direct interaction and real-data usability testing. DD-21–DD-26. Historical preferences qualified.

chapters.notes: Original sales design, eight alternate sales critiques and separate key, CIO, telesales and marketing examples read and inspected. DD-21–DD-28. Static examples are not participant/runtime evidence.

figure_checks.description: Figures4-1 and4-2
figure_checks.inspection: Contrasting intensity isolates the repeated digit while its shape alone does not stand out among other digits. This verifies the attention mechanism, not a measured perception speed.

figure_checks.description: Table4-2 and Figure4-7
figure_checks.inspection: Table separates categorical from quantitative attributes. The two circles demonstrate poor exact area estimation; no empirical accuracy threshold inferred.

figure_checks.description: Figures4-18 and4-19
figure_checks.inspection: Connected nodes group across competing proximity/similarity cues; an enclosure changes the visually dominant grouping in the rightmost example.

figure_checks.description: Figures5-18 and5-19
figure_checks.inspection: Side-by-side designs retain but lighten panel dividers and comparison grids; the example supports selective scaffolding, not removing all nondata marks.

figure_checks.description: Figure5-24
figure_checks.inspection: Historical, year-to-date and current-month ridership occupy three panels with different visibly labeled time intervals. Persistent-versus-situational priority discussion also read.

figure_checks.description: Figures6-6 and6-7
figure_checks.inspection: Horizontal bullet graph displays a zero-origin numeric scale, actual bar, target marker and background ranges. Caption and annotation map each component.

figure_checks.description: Figures6-13 and6-14
figure_checks.inspection: A nonzero-range bullet uses a point instead of a length bar; the following example distinguishes actual quarter-to-date from projected quarter-end quantity.

figure_checks.description: Figures6-24 and6-25
figure_checks.inspection: Stacked segments lack a common comparison baseline except the bottom segment; grouped alternatives change emphasis toward component comparisons.

figure_checks.description: Figure6-28
figure_checks.inspection: Ranked individual contributions appear as bars and their cumulative percentages as a line; accumulation supplies a meaningful connection across named categories.

figure_checks.description: Figures6-31,6-32 and6-33
figure_checks.inspection: Sparkline example combines a reference band and endpoint/current-value cue; the isolated arrow leaves the comparison window ambiguous. The miniature revenue history still needs contextual window/scale disclosure in application.

figure_checks.description: Figure6-38
figure_checks.inspection: Box illustrates quartiles and median with alternative percentile whiskers and separate outliers. This particular whisker convention is not universal.

figure_checks.description: Figure6-41
figure_checks.inspection: Two scatter groups and fitted lines have different slopes; the visual does not establish that slope difference alone is a difference in correlation strength.

figure_checks.description: Figure6-43
figure_checks.inspection: Treemap uses area for revenue and intensity for quota achievement within regional hierarchy. Large red rectangles combine high revenue and low relative attainment, not an independently demonstrated ranking of every business-loss measure.

figure_checks.description: Figures6-56 and6-57
figure_checks.inspection: Single regional chart is expanded to small multiples by sales channel; repeated numeric scales, category alignment and shared legend support comparison.
